# Chapter 10: Cindy

Nancy died in 2004, and the year that followed was a year of firsts—the first Christmas without her, the first birthday, the first ordinary Tuesday that had no special significance but that still carried the weight of her absence. Bob moved through these firsts with the numb determination of a man who had learned, decades ago, that the only way to survive the unbearable was to keep moving.

The widowerhood was its own country, with its own customs and its own geography. Bob
